A position has opened up at the most prestigious travel guide publisher, and you have four weeks in Europe to show that you are the right person for the job. Visit stunning locations, meet locals, get insider tips, collect postcards from famous attractions, and maybe even visit a festival on weekends or fulfill an adventure worthy of a bucket list. Europe awaits you in Abroad, and you need to figure out how you're going to make the most of the opportunity. You'll start with a hand of seven location cards from a deck of 240, as well as a postcard with an endgame goal. Start in your choice of Europe's ten regions. The game lasts four rounds, with each round consisting of seven days. Take turns in a round until you have spent all of your days. On a turn, you can stay where you are, or travel to a new location by plane (by spending money) or by train (be spending energy). Then take one of four activities: 1) Write about the location. 2) Rest, spending a day and three cards to earn 2 energy. 3) Plan, spending a day to draw three cards. 4) Carry out an activity, spending as many days as listed on a card in your hand matching your region. After four rounds, score all your postcards based on whether you met their primary or secondary goal, then see who has logged the most points as evidence of their awesome travel skills. [Rating: 3/10] The idea is good, but the game is not. Very unbalanced cards, bland map and player board design, thin cheap player boards

[Rating: 4/10] This left me pretty unimpressed. As an experience/casual game it can work but don't approach it as a competitive game as players have very limited agency and if you get a bad hand of cards there isn't much one can do...

[Rating: 5/10] Abroad is a somewhat solitary action optimization puzzle with an area majority component. Players are also racing to grab some special achievements before others do, but the central element of the game is your personal calendar in which you play your activities. As a consequence of the solitary puzzly nature of the card play, I found the downtime to be a bit of a bear, especially if you finish your week early because of longer activities.

[Rating: 5.5/10] Turns take too long. Wouldn’t recommend at 5. Area control meets terraforming mars.

[Rating: 6/10] 2 Plays on BGA - its different enough from the other games of its ilk, but I just dont find it that much fun or that it tells a fun story like Lets Go to..

[Rating: 6/10] Played with 5 people.  Liked the calendar mechanism but if a player finished early, they were sitting around waiting for others to finish.  It was crunch because hearts were super hard to come by which frustrated us all.
